highlights.headline: Australia and South Korea’s clean energy deal could boost low-carbon trade
highlights.summary: The deal aims to connect Australia's renewable resources with Korean industries' clean energy demand, potentially transforming a relationship built on coal and gas The post Australia and South Korea’s clean energy deal could boost low-carbon trade appeared first on Climate Home News.

highlights.headline: EU stood firm for ambition and implementation at COP31
highlights.summary: European Commission Joint press release Antalya, 23 Nov 2026 Yesterday at the COP31 UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, the European Union and all 27 Member States in unity showed the world their firm stance to limit global warming through the Paris Agreement and their determination to implement climate commitments already made among global partners.

highlights.headline: Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?
highlights.summary: Germany plans to pay €10 a month into investment accounts for children to encourage long-term retirement saving. Economists say the measure may help build wealth but won't solve the country's pension funding challenge.

items.title: Commission opens formal investigation into possible anticompetitive conduct by Coca-Cola Europacific Partners in the non-alcoholic drinks sector
items.description: European Commission Press release Brussels, 23 Nov 2026 The European Commission has opened a formal antitrust investigation to assess whether Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (‘CCEP') has breached EU competition rules by (i) hindering the cross-border trade of carbonated soft drinks and sports drinks; and (ii) denying certain wholesale customers the possibility to negotiate the procurement of these products on a multi-country basis.

items.title: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate while Montenegro and Albania move closer to membership
items.description: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.
